questions.prompt: During pre-study physiologic calibration, the patient follows the eye-movement instructions. One EOG channel remains nearly flat, but the other EOG channel shows eye movement and the EEG channels appear intact. What is the best next action before lights out?
options: Proceed and annotate the flat EOG channel as a normal finding
Check the affected EOG electrode, connector, impedance and derivation; restore the signal and repeat calibration
Use the intact EOG channel to infer that both EOG electrodes are functioning
Change the EEG montage without first checking the nonresponsive EOG channel
questions.answer: Check the affected EOG electrode, connector, impedance and derivation; restore the signal and repeat calibration
questions.rationale: The failure is specific to a required eye-movement channel during a patient calibration. The technologist should inspect the affected EOG signal path, correct it, and repeat/annotate calibration rather than assuming the patient produced no eye movement.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old has a PSG before a planned MSLT. The recording provides eight hours in bed but only six hours and twenty minutes of sleep. What should the technologist do?
options: Treat this as meeting the pediatric minimum sleep-time protocol
Ignore the PSG because the MSLT uses only daytime data
Flag the short sleep time and communicate with the ordering team under the laboratory's protocol before proceeding
Substitute a home pulse-oximetry result for the missing sleep
questions.answer: Flag the short sleep time and communicate with the ordering team under the laboratory's protocol before proceeding
questions.rationale: The 2024 pediatric MSLT guidance calls for an attended PSG allowing at least eight hours in bed and seven hours of sleep; insufficient sleep requires protocol review.

questions.prompt: An adult is scheduled for MSLT immediately after a split-night study in which PAP pressures were adjusted. Which response best protects test validity?
options: Proceed without noting the titration because the patient slept at least once
Recognize that an MSLT should not follow a PAP-adjustment night and contact the ordering team about rescheduling or further direction
Replace the first nap with an extra ECG lead
Use the overnight recording as the first MSLT nap
questions.answer: Recognize that an MSLT should not follow a PAP-adjustment night and contact the ordering team about rescheduling or further direction
questions.rationale: The adult AASM protocol excludes MSLT after a split-night or initial PAP titration because the preceding sleep and treatment conditions can confound interpretation.

questions.prompt: A nine-year-old child's PSG is found to have respiratory events scored using the adult template solely because the software defaulted to adult criteria. Which correction should the quality reviewer request?
options: Keep the adult template because both adult and pediatric scoring rules are always interchangeable
Review and, where necessary, re-score the respiratory events under the AASM pediatric rules applicable to this age, documenting the correction
Apply adult rules only to REM epochs and pediatric rules only to non-REM epochs
Leave the respiratory event labels unchanged but change the reported patient's age
questions.answer: Review and, where necessary, re-score the respiratory events under the AASM pediatric rules applicable to this age, documenting the correction
questions.rationale: AASM Version 3 FAQ allows optional adult respiratory criteria for children aged 13 or older, not for a nine-year-old. A software default is not authority to substitute adult scoring rules.

questions.prompt: During a diagnostic PSG, nasal-pressure airflow was unavailable from 02:10 to 03:00 because of a disconnected cannula; the channel was restored at 03:00. Which handoff entry best preserves the quality of the recording?
options: All sensors normal by the conclusion of the study; no other technical detail required
Nasal-pressure signal absent from 02:10–03:00; cause, correction and restoration time recorded, with affected data-quality limitations identified
Respiratory scoring was normal for the entire night because the channel later returned
All respiratory channels should be excluded from the entire study because one channel was interrupted
questions.answer: Nasal-pressure signal absent from 02:10–03:00; cause, correction and restoration time recorded, with affected data-quality limitations identified
questions.rationale: A chronological technical record should describe the affected signal, interval, cause, intervention, restored channel and limitation for downstream scoring/review. This is technical documentation, not an independent clinical interpretation.
